## Item 2 — Receipt scan (photograph a receipt into a prefilled transaction)

- **Status:** ⚠️ **FULL REDO BOOKED 2026-08-06, then the grill deliberately WAIVED by the captain the same day.** Booking's ask was a ground-up rethink (entry points, capture, OCR/parsing, inference, duplicate detection, the FAB wheel) with no specific complaint driving it — when the grill opened, the captain's answer was to keep what's already built (**Option B, critique-in-place**, not a blank slate) and skip re-litigating settled ground: *"nothing, just rebuild it for me, and test it for me i wanna see it."* Net effect: **[ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md) stays the design of record, un-superseded.** Slice 2 (`951752c`, history inference + duplicate warning), briefly reverted (`7eaf297`) to give the (ultimately skipped) redo a clean base, is **restored** (`345588e`, 2026-08-06 — a revert-of-the-revert, so its diff is the same change under a new sha, not a rebuild). Remaining work is finishing what was already locked: **Slice 3, the FAB wheel**, then a fresh on-device pass across all three slices.
- **Status (detail):** **Slice 1 ✅ DONE `a312b2f`, real-corpus follow-up `ad40e23e`**, **Slice 2 ✅ DONE `951752c`** (both 2026-08-05, Opus/high; restored 2026-08-06 after the redo-grill was waived, `345588e`) — Slice 3 (FAB wheel) not yet built. Slice 2 needed no grill of its own: it is design-locked by [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md) decision 5 (history inference) and its Consequences (the soft duplicate warning). **Not yet verified on device** — the prior 2026-08-05 on-device note in this doc's history predates the revert/restore cycle; treat as unverified until the fresh pass below runs. ~~GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-29 … not yet built.~~ Design remains as locked: **GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-29 ([ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md)), amended 2026-08-03/2026-08-04 by a second narrow review plus two captain rulings.** ~~⚠️ GATED on Item 5, which is itself ⏸️ DEFERRED 2026-08-03.~~ **Un-gated 2026-08-03 (captain) — no longer gated on [Item 5](#item-5--receipt-scan-de-risking-spike-throwaway-runs-before-item-2-slice-1).** Item 5's spike was extra confidence for the parser design, not a prerequisite to ship: the second review it seeded (`data/ipon-love-receipt-gaps/report.md`) reasoned from the real codebase with `file:line` evidence and resolved seven of Item 5's nine gaps without needing a corpus at all — see Item 5 below for the two that stay corpus-dependent. Item 5 stays open as its own item (its corpus spec and remaining two gaps are still valuable) but **no longer blocks this one.** The design stays locked per ADR-0062 — the follow-up review did not reopen engine, permission or FAB-wheel questions, only entry points, gating and the lifecycle gaps the first grill structurally couldn't reach (see the ADR's amendment note for the full list). **Model: Sonnet, medium effort for the remaining Slice 3 build** (pattern-follow against an already-locked spec; no open design question left) — the original **Opus, high effort** call stands as the record of what Slices 1-2 were built at. **Three slices**, on-device verified between each (see Build order below). **No schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration**, and **no impact on the contract freeze ([v1.7.4.md Item 1](v1.7.4.md#item-1--freeze-the-cross-platform-contract-from-web-phase-0-w2))** — the parser is client-local, mints no deterministic ids, and writes only through existing synced columns.
- **Request:** photograph a receipt and have amount/merchant/date extracted into a prefilled transaction, so logging beats typing. Sourced from a 2026-07-29 competitive gap analysis against the Tarsi budget tracker.
- **Five codebase findings that reshaped the booking** (full detail in the ADR's Context):
  1. **The app has no camera capture at all** — receipts, notes and the couple banner are all *gallery pickers*, and no `CAMERA` permission is declared. "Scan" today means leaving the app entirely.
  2. **`ReceiptStrip` is dead last on the editor form** ([AddTransactionScreen.kt:391](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/AddTransactionScreen.kt#L391)) — which **kills the booking's "converge the two flows" option** as a primary entry: it's found only after the user has typed everything it would have filled.
  3. **The free receipt-photo cap is already 0** ([PlanLimits.kt:42](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/entitlement/PlanLimits.kt#L42), set by v1.6.7 Item 9) — so a premium differential exists without inventing one, which is what settled the gating question.
  4. **The prod APK is 5.1 MB**, making bundled-vs-downloaded OCR a real trade rather than a rounding error.
  5. **Receipts are stored at 1080 px / JPEG 85** — below reliable thermal-print legibility, so OCR must run *upstream* of the compression pipeline.
- **Change (locked — rationale and rejected alternatives in [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md), do not restate here; the second review's amendments are folded in below by pointer, not restated):**
  - **Engine:** ML Kit Text Recognition v2, Latin, **bundled** (`com.google.mlkit:text-recognition`). ~~~4 MB, 5.1 MB → ~9 MB, measure at build.~~ **Measured 2026-08-04 — see ADR-0062 decision 1:** arm64-v8a +11.90 MiB, armeabi-v7a +7.82 MiB. The ADR's own ~9 MB revisit trigger fired and was resolved by the captain — bundled engine kept, size accepted. Buys always-works-offline with no Play Services dependency and no "getting ready" state.
  - **Capture:** `TakePicture` + `FileProvider`, and **`CAMERA` is deliberately never declared** — `ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE` only requires it if declared.
  - **Two entry points:** ~~a scan CTA at the top of the New transaction form, opening a camera-or-gallery chooser~~ **changed 2026-08-04 — see ADR-0062 decision 3:** **two buttons side by side** at the top of the New transaction form — `Scan receipt` (camera) and `From gallery` (picker) — no chooser sheet, taking Slice 1 from four steps to three. Plus a **scrollable FAB wheel** on Records (`＋` armed by default, `📷` peeking smaller; swipe to arm, small buttons directly tappable, **always resets to `＋`**, generic over an action list so voice slots in as a third) — unchanged by the second review. Coach mark per [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-coach-mark-coverage-is-discoverability-triage.md).
  - **Read** `Amount` / `Date` / merchant→`Note`, `Type` forced `EXPENSE`; **inferred** `Category` + `Account` from the user's **own transaction history** (no new schema, no merchant table, no LLM). **Only the inferred fields are captioned** — the read ones are verifiable against the photo shown at the top of the form.
  - ~~**Not gated** — no new `Feature` entry. Premium keeps the photo, free has it read and dropped; structurally the Export CSV-stays-free decision repeated.~~ **REVERSED 2026-08-03 — see ADR-0062 decision 6.** Both entry buttons are **fully paywalled**: the governing reading is the one [Item 3](#item-3--voice-command-natural-language-voice-input-to-log-a-transaction) already states for voice — convenience layered on recording, not recording itself. A new `Feature` entry is needed (described here and in [subscription-paywall-design.md](subscription-paywall-design.md) §8, not built — no enum entry, no `PremiumGate` wiring in this doc pass). `PlanLimits.maxReceiptPhotos` now governs only manually attached photos, not the scan flow. The gate ships **dormant**, per the standing build stance.
  - **Photo goes two places:** in-app attachment (capped, premium-differentiated) and a **`Pictures/Love, Ipon`** gallery copy (free, never gated, **Settings → Finance toggle, default ON**, **written on Save, camera leg only** — timing pinned 2026-08-03, previously unanswered; see ADR-0062 decision 7). The gallery copy forces **the feature's only manifest change** — `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` with `android:maxSdkVersion="28"`, runtime-requested on API 26–28 only.
  - **Failed read stays in the camera** — "Couldn't read that one" → Retake / Enter manually. A *partial* read is not a failure.
  - **New, 2026-08-03 — see ADR-0062 decisions 9–10:** the capture temp file (`cacheDir/scans/{uuid}.jpg`) is deleted after compress, on retake, and by an **age-based (one hour)** startup sweep — never an unconditional one, which would delete an in-flight capture on process death behind the camera. **The same reasoning extends to Item 14's `filesDir/receipts` orphan sweep (added 2026-08-05):** a draft's compressed receipts have no `transaction_images` row yet, so an unconditional sweep would delete a restored draft's own photo after a process death behind the camera — it is now age-guarded (24 h) as the process-death backstop, with the editor ViewModel deleting its unsaved receipts outright on the abandon path, which is the ordinary case. EXIF is applied for recognition via `InputImage.fromFilePath` and fixed for storage with `ExifInterface` + `Matrix` in `CompressReceiptUseCase`, which today silently strips it (a live pre-existing bug this slice fixes as it makes the case routine).
- **Build order (three slices, on-device verified between each):**
  1. **Scan → filled form** — dependency, capture via the two direct entry buttons (no chooser — decision 3), OCR, parser, review with the photo shown, retake, attach via the existing cap path (now gated — decision 6), gallery save + its Settings toggle (timing pinned — decision 7), the `cacheDir/scans` temp-file lifecycle (decision 9) and the EXIF fix (decision 10). **This slice alone is the feature end-to-end, and its on-device pass now doubles as the PH thermal-print go/no-go [Item 5](#item-5--receipt-scan-de-risking-spike-throwaway-runs-before-item-2-slice-1)'s deferred spike would have answered** — see Item 5's Status below.
  2. **Learns from you** — history inference for `Category` + `Account`, with the "from your last SM Supermarket visit" captions, plus a soft, non-blocking duplicate-scan warning (same-type/same-amount/±1-day match against the user's own transactions — warns inline on the review form, never blocks Save; ADR-0062 Consequences).
  3. **The FAB wheel** — the Records door, generic over an action list, plus its coach mark. Unchanged by the second review.
- **Explicitly NOT in this item:** cropping or edge detection (retake is the fix), an LLM parser, a hardcoded PH merchant table, ~~a premium gate on scanning~~ (**reversed 2026-08-03 — scanning is now gated, see above**), persisting the FAB's armed action, the third (voice) wheel slot — which stays with [Item 3](#item-3--voice-command-natural-language-voice-input-to-log-a-transaction) until Horizon #3 un-defers it — and **line-item split: one receipt is one transaction, permanently** (confirmed deliberate 2026-08-03, not an oversight — see ADR-0062 Consequences for why reversing it later is a schema change plus a contract-freeze interaction).
- **Verify:** build green; **tier-1 tests required** on the two pure pieces — the parser (total-line selection against `CASH`/`CHANGE`/`VATable` decoys, ambiguous `07/08/2026` month-first resolution plus the not-future/not-older-than-18-months bound, merchant cleaning) and the history matcher (normalisation incl. `#0142` branch codes, token-subset matching, most-frequent-then-most-recent tie-break, own-rows-only). Both are deterministic given fixed recognised text, so the OCR call itself needn't be mocked deep. On-device per slice, and **the "it got it wrong" edit path is mandatory, not just the golden path** — including a deliberately bad frame to exercise Retake, a first-scan-at-a-new-merchant (nothing inferred), and a second scan at the same merchant (inference now fires). **Slice 1's on-device pass is now the PH thermal-print go/no-go** (folding in Item 5's deferred spike, below) — it must additionally cover a thermal convenience-store receipt (7-Eleven) shot in ordinary indoor light alongside the golden GCash/Maya-screenshot control, a machine-printed supermarket receipt, an SC/PWD discount line, a no-total-keyword receipt, a deliberately bad frame, a bottom-of-receipt-out-of-frame shot, a rotated capture, backing out after scanning (nothing left in the gallery, and the draft's `filesDir/receipts` file gone **at back-out**, not merely by the next cold start — the ViewModel is that file's owner until save; the startup sweep is now age-guarded and deliberately will *not* collect it), killing the app while the camera is open (the process-death path decision 9 exists for), the gallery toggle OFF, **enforcement forced ON with a free entitlement — verify the scan is blocked at the CTA, not a photo-drop caption** (decision 6's reversal), and the same receipt scanned twice. Record from the thermal case specifically whether amount/date/merchant were read, missed, or read *wrong* — read-wrong is the dangerous outcome. Full checklist and rationale: `data/ipon-love-receipt-gaps/report.md` §6.5. **Slice 2 adds to that same pass:** a first scan at a brand-new merchant (nothing inferred, no caption, and the note it writes is what makes the next one work), a second scan at that merchant (category + account now fill in **with** the caption), a manual change to an inferred field (its caption must retire, that field's alone), a retake after an inference (the previous guess is withdrawn, not left on the form), an inferred field on an account **shared** with the partner (Private is forced off, ADR-0018), the same receipt scanned twice (the warning fires, **and Save still works** — that is the assertion, not the banner), a genuine second same-amount expense on the same day (the warning is a false positive there by design and must not obstruct anything), and editing the amount after a warning (it retracts).
- **Slice 1 build outcome (`a312b2f`, 2026-08-05, Opus/high) — built, tests green, NOT yet on device.** Slice 1 is the feature end-to-end; Slices 2 (history inference + duplicate warning) and 3 (FAB wheel) are untouched. **No schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration, no contract-freeze impact** — exactly as the ADR predicted. Suite green at **1365** (+37: parser amount/date/merchant, temp-store age predicate). Six things worth carrying forward:
  1. **The no-`CAMERA` invariant was verified against the built APK, not assumed.** ADR-0062 decision 2 says a future edit adding `CAMERA` silently regresses the design — but the sharper risk was that **ML Kit's own manifest merge** might contribute one. It does not: `aapt2 dump permissions` on the staging APK shows the four original permissions plus `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion='28'` and nothing else, with no camera `uses-feature` either. **Re-run that dump if the ML Kit version is ever bumped** — it is the only check that catches a merged-in permission.
  2. **Exclusion keywords are anchored to the *start* of the line, not matched anywhere in it.** This was the one parser rule the ADR left underspecified, and the naive reading breaks a real case: `TOTAL (VAT INCLUSIVE)` contains `vat` and would be thrown away by a contains-match. Start-anchoring keeps it while still rejecting `VAT 12%`, `CASH …`, `CHANGE …`. Receipt lines are `LABEL … amount`, so the label is at the front — the rule generalises.
  3. **The two-tier money regex is deliberately asymmetric.** The keyword tier accepts a loose number (it already knows the line is a total, so `TOTAL 750` with no decimals reads); the blind last-number fallback demands the strict two-decimal shape, so a TIN, an OR number or a branch code can never pass as an amount. Gap 3's "does last-number hold on a sari-sari scrap" stays corpus-dependent and unanswered.
  4. **A day-first date that cannot be read month-first is salvaged rather than dropped** (`25/12/2025` → 25 Dec, unambiguous by construction). But a month-first date that parses and then *fails the bound* is dropped outright, never retried day-first — that is the ADR's "falls back to today", and retrying would turn a bad OCR read into a confident wrong date.
  5. **Two defects were found by reviewing the diff, not by the tests.** (a) Tapping `Scan receipt` twice in a row stranded the first temp file — the capture is deliberately *held* after a failed read and after a successful one when the gallery toggle is ON, so minting a new one without releasing the old re-opened [v1.7.0 Item 14](v1.7.0.md#item-14--orphaned-receipt-files-are-never-cleaned-up-device-storage-leak)'s leak class. All five release sites now funnel through one `releaseScanTemp()`. (b) Receipt compression ran on the **main thread** — pre-existing on the manual attach path, but this slice makes it routine with full-resolution camera frames on the low-RAM devices the feature targets, so it moved to IO on the same reasoning ADR-0062 decision 10 uses to justify fixing the EXIF bug here.
  6. **`RecognizedLine` (text + bounding-box top/height) is the seam that keeps the parser JVM-testable.** ML Kit is never mocked; `ReceiptTextRecognizer` sorts blocks into reading order (ML Kit guarantees none) and the parser is pure. Slice 2's history matcher should reuse this shape rather than reaching for ML Kit types.
- **Slice 1 deviations from the letter of the ADR, all deliberate:** (1) the scan row is hidden when *editing* an existing transaction — prefilling over data the user already saved is not what decision 3 describes; (2) a successful scan that cannot attach its photo because the receipt-photo cap is full fills the fields anyway and skips the attach silently, rather than raising a cap upsell mid-scan (unreachable while dormant); (3) the split failure copy from Item 5 gap 5 is reconciled with decision 8 as: *nothing usable at all* → the Retake / Enter manually dialog; *text read but no total* → the form opens with an inline framing hint, since decision 8 is explicit that a partial read is not a failure.
- **Slice 1 real-corpus follow-up (`ad40e23e`, 2026-08-06, Sonnet/medium) — parser bugs found by scanning ~15 real receipts (personal thermal prints + phone-camera photos, both PDF scans and JPGs), not synthetic ones. Answers gap 3's open "does last-number hold on a sari-sari scrap" question from the Verify section above: no — several real cases needed fixing, one is still open.** Three distinct bugs, all confirmed against real ML Kit output, not hypothesised:
  1. **ML Kit routinely splits one printed row into two `RecognizedLine`s when the gap between columns is wide** — a receipt's `LABEL … amount` shape, which the whole parser assumes is one line, silently isn't. `RecognizedLine` gained `left` (ML Kit's bounding-box x, previously discarded) so a new merge pass can reassemble same-row fragments by vertical overlap before the existing amount/date/merchant rules run unchanged. Without this, the real total was dropped and a decoy won instead — worse than the graceful blank the parser is designed around.
  2. **Within a keyword rank, a decimal amount now beats a bare integer before the later-line tie-break applies.** A basket-count line (`Total Items: 3`) is supposed to be excluded by [isCountLine], but a real OCR misspelling (`Items` → `Itens`) let it slip past that guard and, post-merge, win on "ties go to later" alone, prefilling `3` instead of the real total. Also fixed: the money regex now takes the *longest* match on a line instead of the last one — a misread decimal point (`532.O0`, the `O` a misread `0`) was splitting into two matches (`532` and a stray `0`) and losing the real digits to the last-match rule.
  3. **Merchant only fills `Note` (and seeds Slice 2's history matcher) when it clears a cheap confidence bar** — real testing found the tallest top-third line is often a TIN, a VAT registration line, or (after fix 1's merge) two unrelated fragments glued together, and a wrong `Note` is worse than a blank one since it also poisons the next history match. Bar: no colon (catches `TIN:`, `VAT Reg TIN:`, a handwritten `Name:` fragment) and no more than ~30% digit characters. A rejected candidate falls through to the next-tallest line in the top third rather than the field going straight to blank — this is also what fixes a merchant regression fix 1 introduced on its own (a merged registration line became tall enough to beat the real header).
  - **One known remaining gap, not fixed:** a receipt where ML Kit failed to recognise a VAT-amount *label* at all (not merged away — genuinely never read), so the exclusion guard that depends on seeing that label never got a chance to fire. Parser-side fixes can't reach this; would need image preprocessing or an OCR-config change, out of scope for this pass.
  - Real-photo testing surfaced a separate, non-parser finding worth carrying forward: **several of the personal test images were app screenshots (ride-hailing/e-wallet confirmations), not photographed paper receipts at all** — a fundamentally different input shape (status bars, booking IDs, no `TOTAL` keyword) the parser was never designed for. Amount happened to still work on those; merchant did not.
  - Unit tests added for all three fixes plus the merchant-confidence filter, reproducing the real recognised-line shapes captured from on-device runs. No schema change, no Room change, nothing outside `ReceiptParser`/`RecognizedLine`/`ReceiptTextRecognizer`.

- **Slice 2 build outcome (`951752c`, 2026-08-05, Opus/high) — built, tests green, VERIFIED on device.** "Learns from you": `Category` and `Account` are inferred from the user's own history with the "From your last SM Supermarket visit" caption, and a same-amount/±1-day match now raises an inline warning that never blocks Save. **No schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration, no contract-freeze impact** — two new *read* queries against the existing `transactions` table, exactly as decision 5 promised. Suite green at **1401** (+36: history matcher, duplicate detector, the two repository reads). Six things worth carrying forward:
  1. **The amount comparison cannot be pushed into SQL, and that is a storage fact, not a preference.** Money is persisted as a plain string (`IponConverters.bigDecimalToString`), so `750` and `750.00` are unequal to both SQL and `equals` while being equal in value — a `WHERE amount = :amount` duplicate check would silently miss the exact case it exists for. The query fetches a date window and `ReceiptDuplicateDetector` narrows it with `BigDecimal.compareTo`. **Any future "find rows with this amount" query has the same trap.**
  2. **Inference only fills a field the user left empty — the opposite of the read fields, which overwrite.** Slice 1's amount/date/note overwrite because the receipt photo sits at the top of the form and makes them verifiable by looking; category and account appear nowhere on the paper, so an explicit choice has to outrank a suggestion. It also only sets an id that still names a live option, so a category deleted since that visit can't leave the draft pointing at nothing with a caption vouching for it.
  3. **A new read supersedes the old guess, so `retractInference()` runs at the top of `processScan`** — clearing *only* fields still flagged as inferred. Without it a retake, or a second scan at a different merchant, would find Category and Account already filled by the read it just replaced and infer nothing at all. This was found by reasoning about the retake path, not by a test.
  4. **The inferred account goes through `TransactionEditorReducer.onAccount`, never a bare `copy`** — an inferred selection is still a selection, so picking a shared account must force the row non-private ([ADR-0018](../adr/0018-shared-accounts-and-categories.md)) exactly as a tap would.
  5. **`runCatching` around a suspending call swallows `CancellationException`.** Slice 1 used it twice on the scan path; a scan cancelled by the user backing out would have carried on into the next step against a ViewModel being torn down. Replaced with a `catchingNonCancellation` helper that rethrows it — a drive-by fix to Slice 1's own two sites, since Slice 2 was about to add two more.
  6. **The ±1 day window is PH *calendar* days, not a rolling 24 hours** — 23:30 last night and 00:15 this morning are 45 minutes apart and correctly *are* a match; 23:45 today and 00:30 two days on are closer in clock time and correctly are *not*. `PH_ZONE` was hoisted out of `ScanReceiptUseCase` into `core/date/PhCalendar.kt` so the scanner's date bound and this window key on the one zone the frozen contract §4 names.
- **Slice 2 deviations / accepted limits, all deliberate:** (1) the history read is capped at the 500 most recent note-bearing own expenses — bounded because it runs on a tap on low-RAM devices for a *suggestion*, and recency is the right bias anyway; (2) the inference captions and the duplicate warning are **not** mirrored into `SavedStateHandle`, so a process death mid-review loses them while the field values themselves survive — the restored value then reads as the user's own choice, which is the safe direction (nothing gets silently wiped); (3) the duplicate warning is computed once per scan and retracted when the user edits amount, date or type, rather than re-queried on every keystroke — it names a specific amount and day, so it must never outlive them.

- **Related, booked later:** [Item 8](#item-8--transaction-drafts-a-parking-area-inside-records-third-exit-from-the-new-transaction-form) proposes a drafts/parking-area feature that would add a third exit (`Save as draft`) to the New transaction form this item builds. Booked 2026-08-04, ~~**not yet grilled**~~ **grilled 2026-08-05 ([ADR-0066](../adr/0066-transaction-drafts-parking-area.md))** — still does not gate this item, and Slice 1 above proceeds independently of it. **One dependency now runs the other way:** ADR-0066 decision 7 amends this item's [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md) decision 7 (`Save as draft` also writes the `Pictures/Love, Ipon` copy), so Slice 1 must land that Save-time write before drafts hook into it — an ordering note, not a change to anything decided here.

## Item 3 — Voice command (natural-language voice input to log a transaction)

- **Status:** ⏸️ **DEFERRED 2026-07-29, same day it was booked — returned to [Post-V1 Horizon #3 (AI companion)](project-build-progress.md), which already names "NL transaction entry" as one of its own sub-features.** Not shelved (Alvin actively wants it) and deliberately **not** moved to [deferred.md](deferred.md) — Horizon #3 is its single home, so it doesn't end up half-planned in two places. **Reason:** the research finding below killed the premise it was booked on. It was pulled out of Horizon #3 on the assumption it was independently buildable as a non-AI feature; on Android, for this app's market, it isn't. **Un-defer when** Horizon #3's hybrid funding model (capped app-funded free tier + BYOK) is designed and grilled — that decision, not this item, is the blocker. The stub is kept here rather than deleted because the hardware finding is the valuable output of the work, and it is what a future grill needs to start from. **Model when revived: Opus, high effort.**
- **Request:** log a transaction by voice using natural language (e.g. "Starbucks 250"), matching Tarsi's voice input. Sourced from the same 2026-07-29 competitive gap analysis.
- **Change (open, to be resolved at grill):**
  - **Disambiguate from Horizon #5, "Voice recording storage"** — audio-note recording/storage, ❌ dropped 2026-07-18 (Alvin: no longer wanted), and from CLAUDE.md's "Voice recording" out-of-scope line, which refers to that same dropped feature. This item is different: speech is transcribed to text and immediately discarded, nothing audio is ever stored. CLAUDE.md's out-of-scope list needs a clarifying amendment once this is grilled/locked (same pattern as the CSV/PDF export un-shelving), so a cold-start agent doesn't read "Voice recording" and assume this is blocked too.
  - STT engine: Android's built-in `SpeechRecognizer`/`RecognizerIntent` (free, zero new dependency) vs. a cloud STT service. Note the offline-first tension: on-device recognition exists (`EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE`, API 33+) but availability is device-dependent, and many devices route speech to Google's servers — so "voice works offline" is **not** a promise this can make on Android the way Tarsi makes it on iOS.
  - NL parsing: regex/heuristic extraction (amount + a merchant/category keyword match) vs. LLM-backed parsing. The latter pulls in Horizon #3's AI-companion cost/hybrid-model questions (capped free tier + BYOK) even for this "simple" feature, since Horizon #3 already names "NL transaction entry" as one of its own sub-features.
  - **⚠️ Research finding, 2026-07-29 — the Tarsi comparison does NOT port here, and this is the item's central problem.** Tarsi's voice input is genuinely LLM-backed ("offline AI chat… better understands natural expense and income entries"), running on **Apple Intelligence's on-device foundation model — free to the developer and present on every recent iPhone**. Android has no equivalent for this app's market: the counterpart, **Gemini Nano v3 via ML Kit GenAI, requires ~12GB+ RAM and a flagship chipset** (Snapdragon 8 Elite / 8 Gen 4, Tensor G5) plus AICore — as of mid-2026 roughly Pixel 10, Galaxy S26, OnePlus 15 and a few Oppo/Xiaomi flagships. **Alvin's own Transsion/MTK test device does not qualify, and neither does most of the budget-Android PH mass market this app targets** (see `rom-force-stop-nav-reset` memory for that device's constraints). So the three real options are: (a) heuristics/regex — free, universal, materially dumber than Tarsi's; (b) cloud LLM — per-call cost, breaks the offline-first stance, and cannot be decided independently of Horizon #3's funding model; (c) on-device LLM — free but functional for a small minority of users, i.e. a premium feature that silently doesn't work on the phones most buyers own. **Unlike Item 2, this item cannot be de-risked into a non-AI feature without accepting a visibly worse result than the app it's benchmarked against.** Grill should treat "build a deliberately simpler heuristic version" vs. "defer until Horizon #3 is funded/designed" as the live fork, not just an implementation detail.
  - Account/category resolution: "GCash 250" needs to resolve to a specific account and category from free text — decide whether ambiguous input prompts the user or best-guesses then leaves it editable.
  - Same premium-gating question as Item 2 — convenience layered on recording, not recording itself.
  - No ADR yet.
- **Verify:** build green; tier-1 tests for the NL-parsing usecase (pure Kotlin, given fixed transcribed text — same testability shape as Item 2's OCR parser). On-device check once built, covering at least one ambiguous/misheard input, not just the golden phrase.

But it had **no receipt corpus and no running code**, so it specified a parser against imagined receipts and a capture flow against an imagined lifecycle. A second grill of the same shape cannot fix that; only real input can. Re-grilling was therefore **declined in favour of measuring first**.

ADR-0062 finding 5 already established that receipts are stored *below* reliable thermal-print legibility (1080 px / JPEG 85, [CompressReceiptUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CompressReceiptUseCase.kt)) — this measures the tier above that, the raw full-res frame.

  - **Throwaway branch, never committed, and explicitly NOT Item 2 Slice 1.** No use case, no ViewModel, no parser, no entry point, no nav change.

Status marked per gap:
  1. ✅ **RESOLVED — when is the `Pictures/Love, Ipon` gallery copy written?** ADR-0062 decision 7 sends the photo there, but the draft is *unsaved* until Save — if the copy happens at capture, backing out pollutes the user's gallery with abandoned scans. ~~Unanswered.~~ **Pinned: on Save, camera leg only** — see ADR-0062 decision 7.
  2. ✅ **RESOLVED — who owns the new full-res pre-compression temp file** from `TakePicture` + `FileProvider`? Nothing in ADR-0062 owns its cleanup — and this **re-introduces the exact bug class [v1.7.0 Item 14](v1.7.0.md#item-14--orphaned-receipt-files-are-never-cleaned-up-device-storage-leak) (`161acec`, [CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.kt)) already paid to fix.** **Own lifecycle at `cacheDir/scans`, age-based sweep** — see ADR-0062 decision 9 (its highest-value finding: an unconditional sweep would delete an in-flight capture on process death).

The grill designed against `CASH`/`CHANGE`/`VATable` decoys but assumed a `TOTAL` line exists. **Built now:** a three-tier ladder — keyword line, then last-number-in-reading-order, then blank (never a guess). **Still corpus-dependent:** whether "last number" actually holds on a sari-sari scrap, or is followed by a date/receipt-number/handwritten line — re-verify once photos exist.
  4. 🟡 **PARTIALLY RESOLVED, keyword strings stay corpus-dependent — SC/PWD discount and service-charge lines**, ubiquitous in PH, where "total" and "what I actually paid" diverge — ADR-0062 didn't say which one wins. **Built now:** what left the wallet wins, via a family preference (`AMOUNT DUE`/`TOTAL DUE`/`NET AMOUNT` beats a bare `TOTAL`) plus a later-in-reading-order tie-break — both hold regardless of exact vocabulary. **Still corpus-dependent:** the exact keyword strings PH receipts actually print (does Mercury Drug say `AMOUNT DUE` or something else?).

## Item 6 — Make the project's Claude hooks relocatable

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `c7a3a1f`** (2026-08-03) — **booked retroactively**, after the change rather than before it; recorded here so the work is not invisible outside the git log. **Model: Opus, xhigh effort** — a small diff, but it edits the commit-permission gate itself, where the cost of a subtle mistake is a safety rail that reads as armed and is not. **Repo tooling only — no app code, no schema, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration.**
- **Request:** fell out of consolidating the working checkout — Alvin moved off the standalone `/Users/lovzay/ipon-love` clone to work in `alvin-workspace/projects/ipon-love`, which invalidated every path in `.claude/`.
- **⛔ The problem, and why it needed fixing rather than repointing.** `.claude/settings.json` hardcoded the old checkout in **all eight hook commands**, four permission-allowlist patterns, and `wrap-force-gate.sh`'s own match. It fails **silently**, which is the whole reason to care: with the old directory still present the gates keep executing stale copies of these scripts out of it, watching the wrong repo; delete that directory and every gate stops firing with no error at all — the commit gates, the book gate and the on-device nudges would each read as armed while doing nothing. **One consequence was already live before the move:** these files are tracked, so they propagate into linked worktrees, meaning a dispatched agent's gates were resolving into the personal checkout rather than into its own worktree.
- **Change:**
  - Hook commands use `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` — the same pattern `build-progress-reminder.sh`, `book-gate.sh`, `book-lock-arm.sh` and `pretest-commit-gate.sh` already used internally, so this adopts existing convention rather than introducing one.
  - **Permission-allowlist entries are match patterns, not shell, so no variable expands there.** Writing `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` into them would have looked correct and quietly matched nothing. They use cwd-relative forms instead (`git status*`, `git diff*`, `find . *`), and the absolute `uidump.sh` entry was dropped as redundant beside the relative one directly above it.
  - `wrap-force-gate.sh` resolves the permitted `-C` path from `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (falling back to the git toplevel) and compares it as a **literal string via `case`, not an interpolated regex** — a path containing regex metacharacters would otherwise mis-match silently. The shell-metacharacter rejection above it is unchanged.
  - [wrap-force](../../.claude/skills/wrap-force/SKILL.md) updated so the skill's description of the mechanism still matches the mechanism.
- **Files touched:** `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/wrap-force-gate.sh`, `.claude/skills/wrap-force/SKILL.md`.
- **Verify:** ✅ `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green (unaffected — no app code changed). **The gate was exercised across eleven cases before the commit landed:** it still allows a bare `git add`/`git commit`, a `-C` naming this checkout, and a multi-line message carrying a `Co-Authored-By` trailer; it still refuses a `-C` naming any **other** repo, `push`, `reset --hard`, a chained `; rm -rf`, a `$(...)` substitution, an absent lock, and a stale one. No on-device check — nothing user-facing changed.
- **⚠️ Related, deliberately NOT fixed here — worth its own item.** `app/build.gradle.kts` could not complete Gradle *configuration* without `local.properties`: `storeFile = file(prop("RELEASE_STORE_FILE"))` throws `Cannot convert '' to File` on the empty default, so even a JVM-only unit-test run — which needs no signing — failed on a fresh clone, a CI checkout, or an agent worktree. ~~Unblocked locally by copying `local.properties` into the new checkout, so it is no longer urgent — but every fresh checkout still hits it.~~ **Fixed 2026-08-04 by [Item 9](#item-9--fix-the-jvm-unit-suite-stale-onboarding-fake--unconfigurable-clean-checkout-build)**, which owns the details of the fix.

## Item 7 — Multi-select records via long-press, with bulk delete

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `1e8cee7`** (2026-08-05; grilled + resolved 2026-08-04, [ADR-0064](../adr/0064-bulk-delete-warns-on-settlement-rows.md)). **Not yet verified on device** — see Verify below. **Model: Opus, high effort** — the interaction is ordinary, but what it deletes is not: it crosses soft-delete/tombstone semantics ([ADR-0010](../adr/0010-keep-tombstones-forever.md)), the LWW sync write rule ([ADR-0001](../adr/0001-client-set-updated-at-with-clock-offset.md)/[ADR-0002](../adr/0002-sync-cursor-model.md)), the transfer-fee cascade (ADR-0031), grouped debt settlements ([ADR-0055](../adr/0055-debt-overpay-cascade-guided-allocation.md)) and marked adjustment rows ([ADR-0057](../adr/0057-balance-adjustment-marked-ledger-row.md)). **Confirmed at grill: no schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration** — bulk delete is a new caller over the existing soft-delete path, not a new storage shape.
- **Request:** Alvin, 2026-08-03 — long-press a row in Records to enter a selection mode, tick several records, and delete them in one action. Today deletion is strictly one row at a time, through the per-row kebab menu in [TransactionsScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt) (`menuOpen` → Delete), so clearing out a bad import or a run of test entries is a long grind.
- **What the code already gives us (checked while booking, so the grill started from fact):**
  - The Records row uses a plain `Modifier.clickable` for edit. **No long-press handler exists on it**, and app-wide only three files use `combinedClickable`/`detectTapGestures` (two charts and the calculator bubble), so adding long-press here has **no existing gesture to conflict with**.
  - [DeleteTransactionUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/DeleteTransactionUseCase.kt) is single-id, soft-deletes, and **already cascades**: deleting a transfer also retires its linked fee row (ADR-0031) and, since [Item 11](#item-11--deleting-a-settlement-transaction-retires-its-debtpayment-group), a settlement leg's `DebtPayment` group ([ADR-0065](../adr/0065-settlement-delete-retires-debt-payment-group.md)). It is also atomic now (`LocalTransactionRunner`).
  - **The app had no multi-select pattern before this.** Item 7 introduces one; per ADR-0064 decision 6, its shape is the precedent Notes, Recurring and Budgets are expected to follow if they add multi-select later.
- **✅ Resolved questions (grilled 2026-08-04 — numbering kept from the booking so this stays cross-readable with the archaeology report):**
  1. **Settlement rows: warn and allow.** Selecting an `isSettlement` expense is permitted, not blocked, and Item 7 builds no cascade of its own. Full rationale and rejected alternatives (block; cascade) in [ADR-0064](../adr/0064-bulk-delete-warns-on-settlement-rows.md). ~~The confirmation warns that deleting it returns the money to the balance but leaves the affected debt marked paid; the underlying corruption is explicitly NOT fixed by Item 7.~~ **Superseded 2026-08-05 by [Item 11](#item-11--deleting-a-settlement-transaction-retires-its-debtpayment-group) / [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-settlement-delete-retires-debt-payment-group.md):** the corruption is fixed, in `DeleteTransactionUseCase` — the path Item 7 already reuses — so bulk delete inherits the retirement for free, and the warning copy must be **inverted** when built: the affected debts *reappear as outstanding* on the Partner Debt Tracker, for both partners. Reuse the sentence Reset finances now shows.
  2. **Adjustment rows: allow, no warning, no special-casing.** [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-balance-adjustment-marked-ledger-row.md) decision 1 designed the ledger row precisely so it fails diagnosably — "there are two dated rows in Records and either partner can delete one" is the documented repair path for a double reconciliation, not a hazard to guard against. Behaviour is identical to today's per-row delete.
  3. **Transfer + its fee selected together: harmless, fixed by construction.** The existing cascade re-deletes an already-tombstoned fee row a second time if both are ticked; verified (empirically, against the real classes) to be a spurious `updated_at` bump with no sync conflict — the server receives the row once at its final timestamp, and equal-timestamp echoes resolve `KeepLocal`. Bulk delete dedupes the selection into an effective id set before writing (`selection ∪ { transferFeeTransactionId for each selected transfer }`) so each id is written exactly once, and the confirmation copy names any fee rows pulled in that the user didn't tick directly.
  4. **All-or-nothing**, in one `LocalTransactionRunner.run { }` — the same atomic primitive Reset finances already uses via `bulkRestamp`. A partial bulk delete would leave the user staring at a list where some rows vanished and some didn't with nothing telling them which; retrying a whole-operation failure is one tap. This stays **single-table**, so it does **not** trip the forward rule frozen in [cross-platform-contract.md §9](../web/cross-platform-contract.md#9-atomic-multi-row-writes--android-has-a-primitive-web-doesnt) (which governs all-or-nothing writes *across* tables, per [ADR-0063](../adr/0063-web-v1-is-online-only.md)) — ~~that rule stays unengaged precisely because Q1 declined to cascade~~ **updated 2026-08-05: the inherited settlement retirement (Item 11) does make this write span `transactions` + `partner_debt_payments`, and §9 still stays unengaged** — see [ADR-0065](../adr/0065-settlement-delete-retires-debt-payment-group.md)'s last consequence for why (Android-only application code; web v1 is online-only and only reads the result).
  5. **Accidental-loss protection: a confirmation dialog naming the row count, and no undo.** No undo snackbar, no new restore path, no `SnackbarHost` — this is still a net improvement over today, where single-row delete has neither confirm nor undo. Undo was considered and dropped: `upsertTransaction` cannot un-delete (it preserves an existing tombstone), so undo would need a new repository restore path plus a snackbar host the app has exactly one of (`SubscriptionScreen.kt`), for a safety net rarely reached once the delete has already synced to the partner. The confirmation dialog is the load-bearing net, and it lands *before* the loss.
  6. **Recurring-materialized occurrences are safe from resurrection — verified, but not for the reason the booking assumed.** The booking expected ADR-0010's tombstone-respect to cover this via a cold-pull `is_deleted = false` optimization. **That optimization was never built** — `SupabaseTransactionRemoteSource` pulls every row past the sync cursor with no `is_deleted` filter, so tombstones arrive on a cold sync like anything else. What actually makes this safe: occurrence ids are deterministic (`ruleId:occurrenceDate`), and `materializeTransaction` is insert-if-absent **including tombstones** (`getById` has no `isDeleted` filter) — a deleted occurrence is never re-created by the next materialization pass or by a manual re-confirm.
  7. **Receipt attachments: retained, not orphaned — the booking's framing was backwards.** Bulk delete does not touch `transaction_images` at all, exactly like single delete today. That means attached receipt files are **not** "collectable by [CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.kt)" as the booking assumed — that sweep only reclaims files with **no** `transaction_images` row at all, and the row survives deletion of its transaction. The files are retained indefinitely, which is what makes undo-by-re-adding-the-row possible in principle; cascading image deletion into bulk delete would actively work against that. Pre-existing, unchanged by this item, and correctly out of scope here.
  8. **Partner-owned rows: confirmed out of reach.** Records is own-rows-only (`TransactionDao`'s query filters `userId = :userId`; combined/couple queries are a separate method Records never calls), so selection needs no exclusion logic — it operates on ids already scoped to the user's own rows.
  9. **Selection-mode UI:** long-press any row to enter selection mode (the pressed row starts ticked); tap continues to mean edit outside selection mode and toggles a tick inside it. The header swaps to a contextual bar (`✕  N selected  … 🗑`) rather than trying to coexist with the filter/bell/eye row v1.7.1 Item 17 just tidied. `BackHandler(enabled = selectionMode)` and the ✕ both clear the selection and exit; deselecting the last row exits automatically. Stepping the viewed month or applying/clearing a filter **clears the selection** — the cheapest rule that prevents "delete 12" while rows outside the visible window are invisibly ticked. **Select-all: yes, scoped strictly to currently visible, post-filter rows — never all history.** The blast radius is capped at what the user can actually see on screen; clearing a bad import, the motivating use case, stays one tap. Selection state lives in `TransactionsViewModel` as a `MutableStateFlow<Set<String>>` folded into `TransactionsUiState` via an additional trailing `.combine` (the main combine is already at Kotlin's typed 5-flow ceiling). Discoverability is flagged, not solved here: the Records coach-mark tour was deleted in v1.7.1 Item 20, so long-press currently has no teaching vehicle.
- **Scope:** Records only. Notes, Recurring and Budgets are explicitly out — per ADR-0064 decision 6, if the pattern proves out they get their own items, reusing this one's shape.
- **Change (this is the grill's output, not provisional):** `combinedClickable` on the Records row to enter selection mode; selection state in [TransactionsViewModel](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt)/[TransactionsUiState](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsUiState.kt); a new bulk-delete use case wrapping `LocalTransactionRunner.run { }` over the existing soft-delete path (a new `@Query("... WHERE id IN (:ids)")` fetch on `TransactionDao`, no schema/version impact) rather than a new repository method; a confirmation dialog naming the row count (and settlement/fee consequences per Q1/Q3) before the delete lands; header swap in [TransactionsScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt). See [ADR-0064](../adr/0064-bulk-delete-warns-on-settlement-rows.md) for the settlement-row decision and its rejected alternatives.
- **What shipped (2026-08-05, `1e8cee7`):**
  1. **`RecordsSelection`** (new, `presentation/`) — the pure selection algebra, kept off the ViewModel so the rules are testable without Hilt. Selection mode is not a flag: it *is* a non-empty `Set<String>`, which is what makes "unticking the last row exits" fall out instead of needing its own rule. `toggleAll` is bounded by the `visibleIds` it's handed, so select-all's reach is structural, not a check that could be forgotten.
  2. **`BulkDeleteTransactionsUseCase`** (new, `domain/usecase/`) — adds no delete semantics of its own; it funnels every row through `DeleteTransactionUseCase` and so inherits the ADR-0031 fee cascade *and* [Item 11](#item-11--deleting-a-settlement-transaction-retires-its-debtpayment-group)'s settlement retirement for free, exactly as ADR-0064 decision 4 anticipated. What it adds is one `LocalTransactionRunner.run { }` across the whole selection (Q4) and the **root/effective-id split**: `deletionRoots` (what `DeleteTransactionUseCase` is invoked on — the ticked rows minus any fee row whose own transfer is also ticked) vs `effectiveIds` (everything that ends up tombstoned, incl. dragged-in fees). That is what makes Q3's dedupe real: a transfer ticked *with* its fee writes the fee exactly once, via the cascade, not twice. The plan is recomputed **inside** the transaction on the write path, so a sync landing between the confirmation and the tap can't act on a stale ledger.
  3. **`BulkDeletePlan`** — the confirmation's numbers (`rowCount`, `untickedFeeCount`, `settlementCount`) come from the same planner the write uses, so dialog and outcome can't drift.
  4. **`TransactionDao.getActiveByIds` + `TransactionRepository.getActiveTransactions`** — the one new DAO read ADR-0064's consequences predicted (`WHERE id IN (:ids)`, no schema hash impact). Tombstones filtered at the query, because the domain `Transaction` carries no `isDeleted`.
  5. **ViewModel** — `selectedIds` + `pendingBulkDelete` paired into one `Selection` holder and folded in through a **single trailing `.combine`** (the main combine is at Kotlin's typed 5-flow ceiling). `visibleIds` is derived in the main combine from the rendered `dayGroups`, so select-all's bound is inspectable in the ViewModel rather than assembled in the composable. `clearSelection()` is called by `previousMonth`/`nextMonth`/`applyFilter`/`clearFilter`.
  6. **Screen** — `combinedClickable` on the row (tap = edit outside selection mode, tick inside it; long-press enters with the row ticked); `SelectionTopBar` (`✕  N selected … ☑ 🗑`) *replaces* the title row rather than coexisting with the filter/bell/eye actions; `BackHandler(enabled = selectionMode)`; the FAB and the per-row kebab stand down mid-selection; a ticked row lifts onto the Blush surface with an accent check in its icon squircle. `RecordsTopBar` extracted so the two bars read as the alternatives they are. Confirmation copy uses the **inverted** ADR-0065 warning — the same sentence Reset finances shows.
- **Files touched:** `RecordsSelection.kt`, `BulkDeleteTransactionsUseCase.kt` (both new); `TransactionDao.kt`, `TransactionRepository.kt`, `TransactionRepositoryImpl.kt`, `TransactionsUiState.kt`, `TransactionsViewModel.kt`, `TransactionsScreen.kt`. Five existing test fakes gained the new repository/DAO override.
- **Tests added:** `RecordsSelectionTest` (9) and `BulkDeleteTransactionsUseCaseTest` (12) — long-press/tap/exit-on-last-untick, select-all partial→full→clear and the empty-month no-op, `allVisibleSelected`; the Q3 dedupe both ways (transfer+fee ticked writes the fee once; fee ticked alone still deletes and never cascades back), plan counts for dragged-in fees / settlements / adjustments-without-warning, ids with no live row not overstating the count, the single-atomic-pass assertion, Q6 (a bulk-deleted materialized occurrence stays in `observeMaterializedRecurringIds`), and Q8 (Records' own-rows-only query is what keeps partner rows out of the selectable set). `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green — **1313 tests, 0 failures**; `assembleDebug` green.
- **Verify:** ✅ build green, ✅ tier-1 unit tests green (see above), ✅ **on-device pass done 2026-08-05** on `Medium_Phone`/`emulator-5554` with the paired staging account `testdev15@iponlove.com` (Juan & Maria). Results:
  - **Selection mechanics** ✅ — long-press enters with the row ticked; tap toggles (1→2→1); unticking the last row exits automatically (title reverts to "Records", per-row kebabs and the FAB return); ✕ exits; system Back exits selection *without* leaving Records.
  - **Select-all scoping (decision 6)** ✅ — unfiltered August ticked **5**, exactly the current user's own rows in the viewed month (DB: 5 own + 4 partner in-window, 68 own all-time). With a Type=Expense filter applied it ticked **4**, dropping the transfer. Partner-replicated rows were never reachable (Q8), and nothing outside the viewed month was ever ticked.
  - **Month stepping clears the selection** ✅ — 5 ticked, stepped to July, selection gone.
  - **Filter changes clear the selection** — ⚠️ *not observable on device, by construction*: the contextual bar replaces the title row, so the filter icon (and the "No matches" inline Clear) is unreachable while ticked. `applyFilter`/`clearFilter` still call `clearSelection()` as a backstop; the reachable half — select-all respecting an *already-applied* filter — is verified above.
  - **Q3 fee dedupe** ✅ — transfer ₱5,000 (Cash→Bank, ₱25 fee) ticked **alone** → dialog "Delete 2 records?" + "That includes 1 linked transfer fee you didn't select." Ticked **with** its fee → "2 selected", still "Delete 2 records?", and the fee line correctly absent. After deleting, the fee row's `updated_at` (`1785900012011`) is **byte-identical to its transfer's** — a second write would have forced `prev + 1ms` under the monotonic stamp (ADR-0001), so this is direct evidence the fee was written exactly once.
  - **Q1 settlement warning + inherited retirement** ✅ — settled the ₱1,200 "Doctor's appointment co-pay" debt, then bulk-deleted the settlement row. Dialog showed the **inverted** ADR-0065 sentence verbatim. Afterwards the Partner Debt Tracker showed the debt back to **"₱1,200.00 of ₱1,200.00 left"** with its Settle button, net balance ₱4,500 → ₱3,300. Locally and **on the server**, the `DebtPayment` row (`26305dca`, `payor_txn_id` = the deleted settlement) is `is_deleted = true` at a fresh `server_rev` — which is exactly what the partner's device pulls.
  - **Q2 adjustment** ✅ — a ₱420 balance-adjustment row deleted with "Delete 1 record?" and **no warning**, identical to a plain row.
  - **Multi-row delete + partner convergence** ✅ — 3 ticks (adjustment + transfer + a plain expense) → "Delete 4 records?" (the effective count, incl. the cascaded fee). All 4 tombstoned in one pass, `pending_sync` cleared, and all 5 tombstones confirmed **on the server** with fresh `server_rev`s. *Literal two-device convergence was not shown — only one emulator was available — so the partner side is verified at the server rows both devices read.*
  - **Q6 recurring occurrence** ✅ — confirmed the Electricity occurrence (materialized as `f1f41360-…`), bulk-deleted it: "To confirm" dropped 2 → 1 and the occurrence did **not** resurface, including after a force-stop + cold relaunch (fresh materialization pass + sync).
  - **Q7 receipts retained** ✅ — bulk-deleted a Jul 19 expense carrying 3 receipts. The transaction is tombstoned and pushed; all three `transaction_images` rows are **untouched** — `is_deleted = 0` with `updated_at` unchanged from before the delete, so the files are neither deleted nor orphaned.

## Item 8 — Transaction drafts (a parking area inside Records, third exit from the New transaction form)

*(Numbering note: Item 7 was reserved for separate in-flight work — booked 2026-08-03 in the captain's working copy, not yet committed at the time this item was booked as Item 8 to avoid a collision. That work has since landed above as [Item 7](#item-7--multi-select-records-via-long-press-with-bulk-delete).)*

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `18feaae`** (2026-08-07) — built + **on-device verified** (emulator, staging, paired account; screenshots in the captain's personal folder). ~~✅ **GRILLED + design-locked** (2026-08-05) — not yet built.~~ The grill ran 2026-08-05 (grill-with-docs pass, report at `data/item8-drafts-grill/report.md`); all seven questions below are answered and the design is recorded in **[ADR-0066](../adr/0066-transaction-drafts-parking-area.md)**. **Model: Opus, high effort** (as forecast, for both the grill and the build), per CLAUDE.md's rule: this touches derived balance (ADR-0007), the partner combined view (ADR-0004/0005/0011), sync FK ordering (ADR-0009) — drafts **do** sync (Q4) — and the entitlement/paywall framing (ADR-0044) — a cross-ADR design, not a pattern-follow. **Schema change accepted by Alvin (2026-08-04): "then let it have schema change as it is. we need the drafts."** **Delta as shipped: Room v31 → v32** (one new entity/DAO/`@AutoMigration`), one new Supabase table + own-row RLS + [migration #25](project-build-progress.md#infra-state) (applied + verified live 2026-08-06), and the **frozen [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md) §3.1 amendment landed** (a 24th `SyncTable` entry) plus the §7.6 clarification.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-08-04):** *"I was thinking of having a drafts section inside records, and instead of blocking the user from doing anything else after taking the photo. So, after taking the photo, the user is then back to New Transactions screen, either they fill things up, or cancel or draft."* Intent, in his words: *"a user is usually busy and has only time to sit down and fix things a couple minutes a day or in a week, it's good to have a parking area for these transactions to settle their Love Ipon tracking — so a draft would help them see what's on their queue once they sit down."* *"Drafting a transaction is free, but receipt isn't, so there should be no friction there."* *"We need a draft screen inside records. It will have two tabs, Draft and w/ Receipts, and inside the w/ Receipts is where the user can see their drafts with receipts and settle it there."*
- **Change (~~stub — deliberately open, shape TBD at grill~~ — locked 2026-08-05):**
  - **Entry point.** The New transaction form ([AddTransactionScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/AddTransactionScreen.kt)) gains a third exit alongside today's `Cancel`/`Save`: **`Save as draft`**. This is exactly the screen [Item 2](#item-2--receipt-scan-photograph-a-receipt-into-a-prefilled-transaction) returns the user to after a scan — drafts are the parking mechanism for the case that CTA creates: a photo prefilled the form and the user doesn't have the couple of minutes to finish it right now. **Offered on new transactions only** — hidden when `editor.isEditing`, since drafting an edit would leave a shadow of a row that already counts (ADR-0066 decision 11).
  - **Sequencing — does not gate Item 2 Slice 1.** Slice 1 ships scan → filled-form end-to-end on today's Cancel/Save pair; drafts are an additive third exit layered on later, not a dependency Slice 1 waits on. State this explicitly so nobody blocks the scan work behind an unbuilt drafts feature. (~~already corpus-gated~~ — Item 2 was gated on Item 5's corpus spike when this was written; that gate was removed 2026-08-03, see Item 2's Status. The point stands regardless: drafts don't gate Slice 1 either way.) **Still true after the grill**, with one addition running the other way: **this item amends [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md) decision 7** (gallery copy on draft-save, Q1 below), so Item 2 must land its decision-7 write *before* this item's Slice 2 hooks into it.
  - ~~**Records gains a drafts surface**, two tabs per the request — **Draft** and **w/ Receipts** — with settling a draft happening from the **w/ Receipts** tab.~~ **Overturned at the grill with Alvin's approval (2026-08-05, Q6):** **one** drafts list, with a receipt thumbnail on the row — no second tab. Reached from a pinned **"Drafts (N)"** card on Records.
  - ~~Schema shape, sync/local-only, cleanup-rule coordination, the free/premium framing, and the tab structure are all open — see questions below. **No ADR exists for this yet**~~ — all five are now locked below, and **[ADR-0066](../adr/0066-transaction-drafts-parking-area.md)** is the authoritative record. This item's bullets are the build view; the ADR carries the rationale and the rejected alternatives.
- **The seven open questions — ✅ all resolved 2026-08-05** (originals kept in place per house style; the grill's answer follows each):
  1. **⚠️ Sharp edge — a draft's receipt photo would be deleted before the user ever comes back.** The receipt-scan review locked two cleanup rules: fresh captures swept after roughly an hour, and stored receipt files deleted once no `transaction_images` row points at them ([CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.kt), the [v1.7.0 Item 14](v1.7.0.md#item-14--orphaned-receipt-files-are-never-cleaned-up-device-storage-leak) fix, `161acec`). **A draft has no `transactions` row**, so both sweeps would eat its photo — breaking the feature in exactly the "I'll come back to this next week" case it exists to serve. This is the same gap #2 from [Item 5](#item-5--receipt-scan-de-risking-spike-throwaway-runs-before-item-2-slice-1)'s nine-gap list (who owns the pre-compression temp file) — ~~still-open~~ **resolved 2026-08-03** for the non-draft case (age-based sweep, see ADR-0062 decision 9), but that resolution assumes a transaction row eventually exists; a draft that sits for days is exactly the case its one-hour sweep does not cover. Whatever the grill decides for drafts, the cleanup rules have to learn about them.
     → **✅ Only one sweep needs to learn, and it learns in its caller.** `CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.invoke()` unions the draft-referenced image ids into `knownIds` — **one line**; the pure predicate at [`:32`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.kt#L32) and its existing test are untouched. The **`cacheDir/scans` one-hour sweep needs no change at all**, because `Save as draft` performs ADR-0062 decision 7's gallery-copy write (see the ADR-0062 amendment below), which releases the full-res temp at draft time. Deleting a draft must also release its files. ADR-0066 decisions 6 + 7.
  2. **Schema shape — a flag on `transactions`, or a separate drafts table?** The real fork, because it decides question 3. Record both options; do not pick one here.
     → **✅ A separate `transaction_drafts` table.** The decisive fact is not the query surface but the row shape: `type`/`amount`/`account_id` are all `not null` (`supabase/schema.sql:166-169`) and `TransactionValidator` requires amount > 0, an account, and a category — **a draft may legitimately fail all four**, and forcing an account choice before parking is exactly the friction Alvin ruled out. The flag option therefore forces either permanently-nullable columns on the money table or placeholder junk values. [ADR-0048](../adr/0048-confirm-on-arrival-recurring.md) decision 2 already refused a *cheaper* version of the same trade. ADR-0066 decision 1.
  3. **If drafts live in `transactions`, every money calculation must exclude them.** Derived balance (ADR-0007), analysis aggregations, budget progress, the Glance widget, export ([v1.7.0 Item 6](v1.7.0.md#item-6--general-export-facility-csv--pdf--zip-receipt-photos-included)), and the partner combined view (ADR-0004/0005/0011) — miss one and a parked draft silently counts as money spent. A separate table cannot have this bug by construction.
     → **✅ Moot, by construction — zero exclusion predicates, zero query edits.** The grill enumerated the surface Q2's other branch would have cost (report §3.2): **12 `TransactionDao` queries + 5 domain calculators + export + the budget-alert worker + the `partner_transactions` view**. Two would have bitten hardest: `observeHasAnyTransaction` ([`TransactionDao.kt:47`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/data/local/TransactionDao.kt#L47)), which gates first-run onboarding seeding on emptiness, and `observeCombined` ([`:58-65`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/data/local/TransactionDao.kt#L58)), which carries **no owner filter by design**. ADR-0066 decision 2.
  4. **Do drafts sync, or stay local to the device?** "A parking area for my queue" argues for surviving a lost phone, which makes a draft a synced row the future web client must also understand — pulling in the FK order and deterministic-id rules frozen in [cross-platform-contract.md](../web/cross-platform-contract.md). Local-only is far cheaper but the queue vanishes on a new device. Sub-question: **can a partner ever see a draft?**
     → **✅ The draft *row* syncs; the *photo* does not cross until promotion.** Sitting down to settle the queue increasingly means a laptop, and web is online-only with no local store ([ADR-0063](../adr/0063-web-v1-is-online-only.md)), so a local-only queue fails at the headline scenario. A second device renders `📷 1 receipt — on your other device` from a synced `receipt_count` — **an accepted weak point**, and the one place this design is strictly worse than the rejected flag option. Ids are ordinary **v4 random** (contract §1.5), so **no §1 amendment**. **Sub-question: no — a partner can never see a draft, structurally.** Own-row RLS only, no redacting view, so **ADR-0004/0005/0011 and frozen contract §5.3 need no amendment.** ADR-0066 decisions 3 + 4.
  5. **The free/premium framing has already shifted.** Receipt scanning is **fully paywalled** as of Alvin's 2026-08-03 ruling, so a free user can never produce a draft *with* a receipt — which makes the proposed "w/ Receipts" tab a premium-only surface in practice and needs an empty state for everyone else. Drafts as a parking area for **hand-typed** entries remains genuinely useful to free users, and is probably the stronger pitch. See [subscription-paywall-design.md](subscription-paywall-design.md) + ADR-0044 rather than restating the paywall design here.
     → **✅ Drafts are free and uncapped, with no paywall surface on the drafts screen** — Alvin's own "no friction there." **No new `Feature` entry** (the scan gate already stops a free user at the CTA; a second gate downstream is redundant) and **no `PlanLimits` field** (a cap blocks the "just park it" flow that *is* the feature). `subscription-paywall-design.md` §10.1's locked contract is **unchanged** — only a §8.1 map line. The empty-state problem disappears with Q6's answer. ADR-0066 decision 8.
  6. **Two tabs, or one list with a filter?** If everything under "w/ Receipts" is also a draft, the second tab is a filter on the first, not a sibling. Records' existing filter ([v1.7.0 Item 7](v1.7.0.md#item-7--records-page-filter-feature)) already has a multi-select pattern that could be reused.
     → **✅ One list, receipt as a row thumbnail — no second tab, no filter chip.** ⚠️ **This overturns Alvin's explicit request, and was put to him as such and approved (2026-08-05).** Settling happens by tapping a draft back into the New transaction form *either way*, so the tab bought a filter rather than a different action; it would also have been premium-only in practice (needing an upsell empty state on a friction-reduction screen) and would have collided with the freeze policy for a lapsed user. **Deferred, not rejected:** the "Has receipt" filter chip — build it only if real usage produces long lists. ADR-0066 decision 9.
  7. **What stops the parking area becoming a graveyard?** The app sends budget alerts only today. Worth deciding whether an unfinished-draft count surfaces anywhere the user actually looks.
     → **✅ A pinned "Drafts (N)" card on Records + an age label per row ("parked 12 days ago"). No notification, and no auto-deletion ever.** The card is a direct clone of `PendingConfirmationsCard` ([TransactionsScreen.kt:213-216](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt#L213-L216)) and doubles as the entry point, so it costs nothing extra. [ADR-0048](../adr/0048-confirm-on-arrival-recurring.md) decision 6 chose this same passive shape for pending recurring occurrences and decision 10 deliberately deferred the push — drafts inherit that ruling rather than reopen it; a notification would also need a new id format against **frozen** contract §1b. ADR-0066 decision 10.
- **⚠️ The one finding that would be easy to get wrong: contract §9 looks like it fires on promotion, and it does not.** Promotion writes three tables (`transactions` insert, `transaction_drafts` soft-delete, `transaction_images` inserts), which reads as an all-or-nothing write — and §9's **frozen** forward rule says such a feature *"must be designed as a server-side `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC from the start if web needs to author it"*, which web does. **But the draft's id *is* the future transaction's id** ([TransactionEditorState.kt:15](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionEditorState.kt#L15)), so promotion needs **ordering, not atomicity**: write the transaction first and retire the draft second, and the only failure mode is a stale row in the queue that re-settles as an **idempotent upsert of the same id** — money can never double. The reverse order loses data, so the ordering is a rule binding every client, not a preference. **No RPC, no §9 amendment.** ADR-0066 decision 5.
- ~~**Explicitly NOT in this item:** any code, schema, migration, or ADR — this is a booking stub only.~~ **Superseded 2026-08-05** — the grill has run and produced [ADR-0066](../adr/0066-transaction-drafts-parking-area.md). Still explicitly NOT in this item: **any code**. The build is the next step and has not started.
- **Build order — planned as three slices; shipped as one** (`18feaae`). The three gates below were all met in that single commit, so they are kept as the record of what had to be true rather than as three separate landings:
  1. **Data + domain.** Supabase table + migration + own-row RLS; Room entity/DAO/migration **v31 → v32**; `TransactionDraftRepository`; `SyncTable.TRANSACTION_DRAFTS` (appended **after** `NOTIFICATIONS`, ordinals 1–23 unchanged) + syncer + DTO; `SaveDraftUseCase` / `PromoteDraftUseCase` / `DeleteDraftUseCase`. **Gate:** ✅ unit suite green; a draft round-tripped to the server and back (`server_rev 4382` stamped live, nulls intact).
  2. **The third exit.** `Save as draft` on `AddTransactionScreen` (new transactions only); hydrating a draft back into `TransactionEditorState`; gallery-copy-on-draft-save; `CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase` made draft-aware. **Gate:** ✅ on-device three-way exit — `Cancel` / `Save as draft` / `Save`.
  3. **The surface.** Pinned "Drafts (N)" card on Records + the drafts screen + age labels + receipt thumbnails. **Gate:** ✅ on-device — parked a draft with a receipt, **backdated its file past the 24h sweep guard**, cold-restarted, photo still there (the Q1 regression, tested against the sweep rather than around it).
- **⚠️ One design point moved after the captain's screenshot review (2026-08-07):** `Save as draft` shipped first as a full-width outlined button at the **foot of the form**; Alvin asked for it **beside `Save` in the top bar**, which is where it now lives. It is an **icon** (`BookmarkAdd` + long-press tooltip + `contentDescription`), not a second text button — spelled out next to "Save" it costs ~170dp of the action slot and truncates the title to "New transactio…" on a 360dp screen. Verified at a true 360dp width (`wm density 480`; the emulator's own override is 356 ≈ 485dp, so the tight case had never been exercised).

## Item 9 — Fix the JVM unit suite: stale onboarding fake + unconfigurable clean-checkout build

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `db8a79e`** (+ `bd64d63`, the guard-scoping follow-up, and `e171774`, the `package*`/`install*` broadening) (2026-08-04) — **booked retroactively**, after the change rather than before it (dispatched fix, same convention as Item 6). **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — two independent, mechanical breakages, no design risk. **No app code beyond a test fake, no schema/Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration.**
- **Request:** closes Item 6's "⚠️ Related, deliberately NOT fixed here" note above — a fresh clone, CI runner, or dispatched worker copy still could not even *configure* Gradle without `local.properties`; separately, the suite hadn't *compiled* since 2026-07-28 either. Both had to be fixed before a CI check (the deliberately separate follow-up) could be added at all.
- **Two independent breakages, both blocking `testStagingDebugUnitTest`/`testDebugUnitTest` on a clean checkout:**
  1. **Compile failure since `fc388cf`** ([v1.7.1 Item 19](v1.7.1.md), collapsible "Coming up" card): `OnboardingRepository` gained `observeComingUpCollapsed()`/`setComingUpCollapsed()`, and `ShouldShowOnboardingUseCaseTest`'s anonymous fake was never updated to match, so the module hadn't compiled in over a week. Added trivial `flowOf(false)`/no-op overrides, matching the fake's existing style for its other `Flow`-returning members (e.g. `observePairingCardDismissed()`).
  2. **Configuration failure on any fresh checkout:** `app/build.gradle.kts` called `file(prop("RELEASE_STORE_FILE"))`, which throws `Cannot convert '' to File` on the empty default when `local.properties` is absent — killing Gradle configuration for *every* task, including JVM-only unit tests, exactly as Item 6 flagged. The release `signingConfig` is now only created when all four `RELEASE_*` properties are present (byte-identical behavior to before when they are); a `gradle.taskGraph.whenReady` check fails loudly, before any task executes, when they're absent — it never silently falls through to an unsigned or debug-signed release build. **Scoped to the four verbs that write or deploy a release artifact** (a `^(assemble|bundle|package|install)[A-Za-z0-9]*Release(Bundle)?$` match on the requested task graph, not a bare `"Release"` substring) so it only fires for tasks that actually produce a signed APK/AAB — `lintRelease` and any future release-variant unit test both stay runnable on a keystore-less CI runner, which the substring-matching first draft would have wrongly blocked (caught in review before landing). The `package*`/`install*` verbs were added in a second review pass: the assemble/bundle anchors are not where the artifact is written — `packageStagingRelease` writes the APK and `packageStagingReleaseBundle` the AAB, and `installStagingRelease` depends on the packaged APK rather than on the assemble anchor, so an anchor-only match still let those three routes emit an unsigned artifact and exit 0.
- **Files touched:** `app/build.gradle.kts`, `app/src/test/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/ShouldShowOnboardingUseCaseTest.kt`, `README.md` (the four `RELEASE_*` key names added to the `local.properties` template — names only, no values — so the guard's "see README.md" pointer resolves to something).
- **Verify:** ✅ `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green with **no `local.properties` present** (193 test result files, 0 failures). ✅ `assembleStagingRelease`, `bundleStagingRelease`, `packageStagingRelease` and `packageStagingReleaseBundle` all **fail loudly** (exit 1, clear message naming the missing properties) under the same no-`local.properties` condition, while `lintStagingRelease` and `testStagingDebugUnitTest` still configure clean — checked task-by-task with `--dry-run`, which builds the same task graph the guard inspects. (`installStagingRelease` does not exist at all when the release variant has no signing config, which is exactly the no-properties case; the regex covers the name for when it does.) — confirms constraint 2 (never a silent unsigned/debug-signed release). The properties-*present* path (constraint 1, byte-identical signing) was verified by code inspection only — the guarded block is unchanged from before, just gated behind a condition that is true in that case — not exercised against a real keystore, since fabricating `local.properties`/credentials was explicitly out of scope for this item.
- **Explicitly out of scope, left for the next item:** a CI workflow enforcing this suite — deliberately separate so the build-health fix and the CI gate can be reviewed independently.
